result.rationale: Verifiable in the diff: addGuests.handler.ts computes uniqueGuests by filtering out emails already present in booking.attendees or blacklisted; if uniqueGuests.length is 0 it throws, but if only some are filtered out the handler proceeds, adds only the remaining guests, and returns the hardcoded 'Guests added' message with no per-email feedback. The caller (AddGuestsDialog) shows a generic success toast. So an organizer submitting a mix of new and already-attendee emails is never told which were dropped — silent data/input loss introduced by this change. This is a genuine correctness/UX defect

judged_text: Guests filtered out by the uniqueGuests check (already an attendee, blacklisted, or case-variant) are dropped with no per-email feedback — the response is a hardcoded 'Guests added' regardless of how many were skipped. An organizer submits two emails where one is already an attendee; the toast says 'Guests added', the skipped person is neither added nor notified, and the organizer assumes the colleague is on the booking and misses the meeting.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows partial-success behavior with no per-email feedback: `addGuestsHandler` filters `guests` into `uniqueGuests` (dropping emails already in `booking.attendees` or blacklisted) and proceeds if `uniqueGuests.length > 0`, then always returns `{ message: "Guests added" }` (hardcoded) without reporting skipped addresses. On the client, `AddGuestsDialog` always shows the same success toast `t("guests_added")` on mutation success. So if a submission contains one existing attendee and one new guest, the existing one is silently skipped but the UI still indicates success with no detail. This is a diff-grounded UX/edge-case issue rather than a clear functional defect.
